pr_title: Avoid dialog's window relayout during an ongoing resize event (fix #3747)
pr_body:
Fix #3747 

Also, the first commit fixes an unrelated issue I saw when looking at the code. It is about how the hexpand and vexpand were being set.
pr_comments: It looks like this fix brings back the problems solved in 06a387fd45f288c69213a5cc0b09fdbf742dfdde
I almost give up on this one... 😅
What about now? It is simpler, but not sure if we should check in layout and expandWindow methods

I'm not sure what or how it happened, but today when I tried the latest approach in Linux it didn't even work, I mean, the bug wasn't fixed. So I tested again in macOS...same, the bug was still there, the dialog's height wasn't updated...so...I'm shocked how it seemed to me that it worked last Friday...
I'm going to push a slight change to make it work (I've tested it in Ubuntu 18.04.6 LTS and macOS).
Okay, I was testing this without the UI with multiple windows feature on Linux...when I activate this, I'm able to reproduce what you said. In macOS works either way.

Seems that the issue is not related to this fix as far as I was able to debug in linux. Seems that the problem is because when we ask for the window's size, the message that resized the window didn't arrive yet, so we got the size before resize, then the window size is set to its previous size. To clarify, this is the order of messages:
1. Set new window size
2. Get window size (here we get the old size because the message sent in 1 wasn't processed yet)
3. Set window size using the size of previous step (the window is set again to its original size)

Specifically this is the code where this happens:
https://github.com/aseprite/aseprite/blob/53c851c547fdea3ca94a7b130bfb0fcbf60fffdb/src/app/script/dialog_class.cpp#L171-L178


This also explains why you can see a flickering effect in the window's width.

To fix this I've created https://github.com/aseprite/laf/pull/59
The commit missed (fix #3747), closing the issue manually.

issue_context.title: Modifying the dialog within the `onpaint` method causes it to render with a constant height
issue_context.body:
Demo code to replicate the issue:

```lua
if app.apiVersion < 21 then
    print("API version is lower than 21")
    return
end

local dialog = Dialog("Canvas Resize Test")

dialog --
:canvas{
    width = 200,
    height = 200,
    onpaint = function(ev)
        local context = ev.context

        dialog --
        :modify{id = "canvas-width", text = tostring(context.width)} --
        :modify{id = "canvas-height", text = tostring(context.height)}
    end
} --
:label{id = "canvas-width", label = "Width:"} --
:label{id = "canvas-height", label = "Height:"} --

dialog:show{wait = false}

```

Preview:

![canvas-modify-issue](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/10217876/224553985-7b47eb93-33df-4120-b276-357b63b93033.gif)

### Aseprite and System version

* Aseprite version: 1.3-rc1-x64, Steam
* System: Windows 11

review_comments: I think this commit (4c3bec448a784df829156829e90251b1898ead04) is not necessary (check that `hexpand = lua_toboolean(L, -2);` uses `-2` to access to the first `lua_getfield(..."hexpand")`). Both codes do the same I think.
